name: Claude Code

routes.api_key: Official binary speaks Anthropic Messages to Lamp's broker (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL); the provider key stays in the broker.
routes.subscription: Native setup-token sign-in held only on an owner-designated custody host (CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN); T21 custody path.

native_subagents: Task/Agent tool when native_subagents is enrolled; each reported as an observed child session (parent_tool_use_id). Otherwise disabled and Lamp spawn is used.
limitations: Subscription use is subject to Anthropic's consumer and Commercial Terms for the account; Lamp never proxies or refreshes the subscription token.
API turns via broker were demonstrated with an OpenRouter zero-price route, not Anthropic's own endpoint.

name: Codex CLI

routes.api_key: Official binary uses a custom model_provider (wire_api=responses) pointed at Lamp's broker; key stays in the broker.
routes.subscription: Native ChatGPT device sign-in into the session's own CODEX_HOME on the custody host; VM-owned refresh, never copied between hosts.

continuation: codex exec resume <thread_id>; thread_id from thread.started
native_subagents: multi_agent feature when native_subagents is enrolled; collab_tool_call receiver threads reported as observed child sessions. Otherwise disabled.
limitations: ChatGPT plan rate limits apply to subscription turns.

name: opencode

routes.api_key: Official binary with an OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT provider (@ai-sdk/openai-compatible) pointed at the broker's native chat-completions route.

endpoints: provider API chosen by the owner
native_subagents: General sub-agent (task tool) when native_subagents is enrolled. Each runs as its own opencode child session; its sessionId and output come from the task tool's metadata and result, and it uses the parent's model route and grant, so its usage is charged to the parent's budget. Each is reported as an observed child session. Without the flag it is disabled and Lamp spawn is used.
limitations: No Anthropic OAuth route: opencode's resurrected Claude subscription login is not a permitted route and is not offered.
Provider subscription routes other than API keys are not enrolled.

name: Cursor CLI (cursor-agent)

routes.api_key: Official CURSOR_API_KEY (user or service account) held on the custody host; traffic goes to Cursor's own backend.
routes.subscription: Documented native 'agent login' into an isolated CURSOR_CONFIG_DIR on the custody host.

native_subagents: Not exposed by the headless CLI.
limitations: Cursor has no bring-your-own-endpoint route; model traffic always goes to Cursor, so the Lamp broker cannot hold the credential.
Needs a Cursor account; not yet signed in for Lamp tests.
On macOS the CLI tries to save the API-key login to the system keychain; Lamp runs it where no keychain is available (Linux hosts and sandboxes).

Vendor credential custody: Lamp runs Cursor with its documented permissions (https://cursor.com/docs/cli/reference/permissions) denying Shell(*), Read(/**), Read(**), Write(/**), Write(**) and WebFetch(*), and allowing only Mcp(lamp:*). Deny rules take precedence over allow rules. The agent works only through Lamp's MCP tools, which run in the sandbox from an environment without credentials. The key (CURSOR_API_KEY) or login stays in custody on the harness host. Lamp refuses a workspace that carries .cursor/ project config, and refuses this route at a sandbox location. On macOS the CLI also tries to save the key to the system keychain, so Lamp runs this route on Linux hosts.

name: GitHub Copilot CLI

routes.api_key: Official BYOK (COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL, type openai) pointed at the broker; COPILOT_OFFLINE so no GitHub entitlement is used.
routes.subscription: Not offered by Lamp (credential custody). Vendor route: Official device login or fine-grained token with the Copilot Requests permission (COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN); separate from any Actions token.

native_subagents: task sub-agents when native_subagents is enrolled. subagent.started/completed/failed events give a stable toolCallId and the sub-agent's totalTokens, and tool.execution_complete gives its result. It uses the parent's model route and grant, so its usage is charged to the parent's budget. Each is reported as an observed child session. Without the flag the task tool is denied and Lamp spawn is used.
limitations: Copilot subscription device login needs the owner to enter a code on github.com; not yet done for Lamp tests.

Lamp does not offer a route that would hand a real vendor credential to the agent: Copilot's GitHub sign-in is a token in its environment (COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN) or its own login file, both reachable by its own tools. The BYOK route takes only an endpoint-scoped broker grant and stays offered.

name: Amp

routes.api_key: Not offered by Lamp (credential custody). Vendor route: Official AMP_API_KEY access token held on the custody host; execution is local (--execute), model traffic goes to ampcode.com.

native_subagents: Amp sub-agents run server-side inside the thread; not separately reported.
limitations: Remote orb execution (--orb-execute) runs on Amp's servers and is not relocated into a Lamp sandbox.
Needs an Amp account access token; not yet created for Lamp tests.
Lamp does not offer a route that would hand a real vendor credential to the agent: Amp takes AMP_API_KEY from its environment or its own login file, both reachable by its own tools.

name: goose

routes.api_key: Direct provider mode (GOOSE_PROVIDER=openai, OPENAI_HOST) pointed at the broker's native chat-completions route.
routes.delegated: ACP mode delegates sign-in and transport to another official harness; no continuation is claimed for it.

endpoints: provider API chosen by the owner
native_subagents: delegate sub-agents when native_subagents is enrolled. The delegate tool's result names the sub-agent session (_meta.subagent_session_id), and goose's notifications report when it runs and ends. It uses the parent's provider route and grant, so its usage is charged to the parent's budget. Each is reported as an observed child session. Goose streams no separate sub-agent transcript in run mode; only its run and end notices are relayed.
limitations: ACP-delegated sessions inherit the delegate's continuation; goose itself cannot resume them.

name: Gemini CLI

routes.api_key: Not offered by Lamp (credential custody). Vendor route: Official GEMINI_API_KEY (AI Studio) or Vertex credentials held on the custody host; traffic goes to Google.
routes.subscription: Not offered by Lamp (credential custody). Vendor route: Google sign-in only where the account's current eligibility allows it; checked per account, not assumed.

limitations: Lamp's broker does not speak the Gemini API wire format, so the key is held on the custody host rather than in the broker.
Google rejects automated browser sign-in; an API key must be created by the owner.

Lamp does not offer a route that would hand a real vendor credential to the agent: Gemini CLI takes GEMINI_API_KEY from its environment or a Google login from its own home, both reachable by its own tools.

name: pi

routes.api_key: Pinned provider in models.json (api openai-completions) pointed at the broker's native chat-completions route.

endpoints: provider API chosen by the owner
continuation: pi -p --session-id <uuid> (Lamp chooses the ID before the first turn)
limitations: No universal subscription entitlement; each provider's own route applies.

name: Devin CLI

routes.subscription: Official 'devin auth login' (manual token flow) into the session's isolated home on the custody host; local execution.
routes.api_key: Official service API key where the account provides one.

continuation: devin -p --resume <session_id>; ID read from 'devin list --format json'
native_subagents: Not exposed by the local CLI.
limitations: Cloud sessions (--cloud) run on Devin's machines; Lamp does not relocate them into a sandbox and does not present a cloud session as local.
Headless output is plain text only.
Use speed:standard; Devin's daily quota is shared.

Devin reads its device login only from $XDG_DATA_HOME/devin/credentials.toml and does not take the login's key from WINDSURF_API_KEY, so Lamp runs it with that login in place on its own host. DEVIN_SESSIONS_DIR keeps sessions in the Lamp session home. Print mode needs --respect-workspace-trust false.

Vendor credential custody: Lamp runs Devin with its documented permissions (https://docs.devin.ai/cli/reference/permissions) denying its read, edit, grep, glob and exec tools and web fetch, and allowing only mcp__lamp__*. A deny rule always wins. Project config outranks user config, so Lamp refuses a workspace that carries .devin/. The device login is used in place from $XDG_DATA_HOME/devin/credentials.toml, or WINDSURF_API_KEY stays in custody. The agent works only through Lamp's MCP tools in the sandbox. Lamp refuses this route at a sandbox location. Not run with these rules: the owner's Devin login was deleted after the section 7 run.

name: Factory Droid

routes.api_key: Factory's documented BYOK custom model (generic-chat-completion-api) pointed at the broker; no Factory login is needed for this route.
routes.subscription: Official FACTORY_API_KEY or native login on the custody host for Factory-hosted models.

native_subagents: Task/SpawnAgent when native_subagents is enrolled. Each call ID is reported as an observed child session with its result. On the BYOK route without a Factory sign-in, droid 1.6.0 refuses to start the sub-agent session (daemon reason missing_authed_user_or_org), so the child ends with that error. Native droid sub-agents need a Factory account. Without the flag Task/SpawnAgent are removed and Lamp spawn is used.
limitations: BYOK turns reach only the configured model endpoint (observed: no Factory host contacted from a vendor-only VM); Factory-hosted models need the owner's Factory key, not yet provided for Lamp tests.

Vendor credential custody: Lamp runs droid's Factory-hosted route with --only-tools MCP:lamp (https://docs.factory.ai/cli/configuration/mcp), so droid has only Lamp's MCP tools, which run in the sandbox. FACTORY_API_KEY stays in custody on the harness host. Project and ancestor .factory/ config (mcp.json, hooks.json) is refused, as is this route at a sandbox location. Not run: no Factory credential is available without reading the owner's macOS keychain.
